# ghost_repository (Resource)

Manages a Ghost repository.

Repositories are created through the GitHub-compatible API and updated or deleted through Ghost's native API.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A private repository owned by the authenticated user.
resource "ghost_repository" "example" {
  name        = "example"
  description = "Managed by Terraform"
}

# A public repository in an organization, initialised with a commit. A
# default_branch can only be set to a branch that exists, which on a new
# repository needs auto_init.
resource "ghost_repository" "org" {
  name               = "org-example"
  owner              = "my-org"
  visibility         = "public"
  auto_init          = true
  default_branch     = "main"
  gitignore_template = "Go"
  license_template   = "mit"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The repository name. Ghost derives the slug from it, so renaming also changes `slug` and the repository URL. The Ghost API reports the slug rather than the display name, so importing a repository whose display name differs from its slug shows a one-time in-place rename.

### Optional

- `auto_init` (Boolean) Create an initial commit when the repository is created. Changing it forces a new repository, except when it was unset (e.g. after import).
- `default_branch` (String) The default branch. The branch must already exist, so on a new repository this usually needs `auto_init`. `ghost_branch_default` manages the same setting: use one or the other, not both. Use `ghost_branch_default` to make a branch created with `ghost_branch` the default, and leave this unset.
- `description` (String) A short description of the repository.
- `gitignore_template` (String) A `.gitignore` template to apply at creation, e.g. `Go` (`ghost_gitignore_templates` lists them; Ghost matches the name case-insensitively). Changing it forces a new repository, except when it was unset (e.g. after import).
- `license_template` (String) A license template to apply at creation, e.g. `mit` (`ghost_licenses` lists the keys; Ghost matches the key case-insensitively, so an SPDX ID such as `MIT` also works). Changing it forces a new repository, except when it was unset (e.g. after import).
- `owner` (String) The user or organization that owns the repository. Defaults to the authenticated user. Changing it (other than its letter case) forces a new repository.
- `visibility` (String) Either `public` or `private`. Defaults to `private`.

### Read-Only

- `clone_url` (String) The HTTPS clone URL.
- `fork` (Boolean) Whether the repository is a fork.
- `full_name` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`.
- `html_url` (String) The repository's web URL.
- `id` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`.
- `node_id` (String) The GraphQL node ID.
- `private` (Boolean) Whether the repository is private.
- `repo_id` (Number) The numeric repository ID.
- `slug` (String) The URL-safe name Ghost derived from `name`.
- `ssh_url` (String) The SSH clone URL, empty when SSH is unavailable.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Repositories are imported by their full name, "owner/slug".
terraform import ghost_repository.example my-user/example
```
